The exegetes differed about who the people of this story were. From Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, it is reported that they were the people of Persia, when their king wanted to make lawful the marrying of close relatives, and their scholars refused him, so he set out to dig a trench and threw into it whoever among them denounced him, and the lawfulness of close marriages continued among them until today.

Also from him: they were a people in Yemen among whom believers and polytheists fought; the believers overcame their disbelievers, then they fought again and the disbelievers overcame the believers, so they dug trenches for them and burned them in them.

Also from him: they were from among the Abyssinians, and their one [i.e., their prophet] was an Abyssinian.

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench, the fire full of fuel﴾: He said: "People from the Children of Israel dug a trench in the earth, then kindled a fire in it, then they stood over that trench with men and women, and they were presented to it. And they claimed that it was Daniel and his companions."

This is also what al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said, and other things have been said. Imam Ahmad said:

Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There was a king among those before you, and he had a sorcerer. When the sorcerer grew old, he said to the king: 'I have grown old and my appointed time has come, so send me a boy to teach him sorcery.' So he sent him a boy, and he taught him sorcery. Between the sorcerer and the king there was a monk, so the boy came upon the monk and heard his speech, and he was pleased with his manner and his speech. Whenever he came to the sorcerer, he would strike him and say: 'What delayed you?' And whenever he came to his family, they would strike him and say: 'What delayed you?' So he complained of that to the monk, who said: 'When the sorcerer wants to strike you, say: "My family detained me." And when your family want to strike you, say: "The sorcerer detained me."

He said: One day, while he was passing by, he came upon a huge, terrifying creature that had blocked the people, so that they could not pass. He said: "Today I will know whether the matter of the monk is more beloved to Allah, or the matter of the sorcerer." He then took a stone and said: "O Allah, if the matter of the monk is more beloved to You and more pleasing to You than the matter of the sorcerer, then kill this creature so that the people may pass." He threw it and killed it, and the people passed on. The monk was informed of this and said: "My son, you are better than me, and you will be tested. If you are tested, do not point to me." The boy used to heal the blind, the leper, and all other diseases, and cure them. A companion of the king had gone blind, so he heard about him and came to him with many gifts, saying: "Cure me, and all of this here will be yours." He replied: "I do not cure anyone. Only Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cures. If you believe in Him, I will supplicate to Allah, and He will cure you." He believed, supplicated to Allah, and Allah cured him. Then he went to the king and sat in his usual place. The king said to him: "O so-and-so, who restored your sight?" He said: "My Lord." He said: "Me?" He said: "No, my Lord and your Lord is Allah." He said: "Do you have a lord other than me?" He said: "Yes, my Lord and your Lord is Allah." He kept torturing him until he pointed to the boy. He sent for the boy and said: "My son, has your sorcery reached the point where you can cure the blind, the leper, and these diseases?" He said: "I do not cure anyone. Only Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cures." He said: "Me?" He said: "No." He said: "Do you have a lord other than me?" He said: "My Lord and your Lord is Allah." So he tortured him also, until he pointed to the monk. The monk was brought, and the king said: "Turn back from your religion." He refused, so he placed the saw at the middle of his head until his two halves fell apart. Then he said to the blind man: "Turn back from your religion." He refused, so he placed the saw at the middle of his head until his two halves fell to the ground. He said to the boy: "Turn back from your religion." He refused, so he sent him with a group of men to such-and-such mountain, saying: "When you reach its peak, if he turns back from his religion, (good); otherwise, throw him down [from above]." [[Addition from the Musnad.]] They took him away, and when they reached the top of the mountain, he said: "O Allah, suffice me against them however You wish." The mountain shook under them, and they all were thrown down. The boy came walking until he entered upon the king and said: "What did your companions do?" He said: "Allah has sufficed me against them." So the king sent him with a group in a small boat, saying: "When you take him out into the middle of the sea, if he turns back from his religion, (good); otherwise, drown him in the sea." They took him out into the middle of the sea, and the boy said: "O Allah, suffice me against them however You wish." They all drowned, and the boy came until he entered upon the king and said: "What did your companions do?" He said: "Allah has sufficed me against them." Then he said to the king: "You will not kill me until you do what I command you. If you do what I command you, you will kill me; otherwise, you will not be able to kill me." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "Gather the people in one open place, then crucify me on a trunk, take an arrow from my quiver, and say: 'In the name of Allah, Lord of the boy.' For when you do that, you will kill me." He did so, placed the arrow in the middle of his bow, threw it, and said: "In the name of Allah, Lord of the boy." The arrow struck his temple, and the boy placed his hand on the spot where the arrow had struck and died. The people said: "We believe in the Lord of the boy." It was said to the king: "Have you seen what you were fearing? By Allah, it has come upon you. All the people have believed." So he ordered that trenches be dug at the mouths of the alleys, the trenches were dug, fires were kindled in them, and he said: "Whoever turns back from his religion, let him go; otherwise, throw him into them." He said: "They were pushing and shoving one another into them. Then a woman came with a son of hers whom she was nursing, and it seemed she hesitated to fall into the fire. The child said: 'Be patient, O mother, for you are upon the truth.'"

This is how Muslim related it at the end of his Sahih, from Hudbah ibn Khalid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with similar wording. [[Musnad (6/16) and Sahih Muslim, no. (3005).]] An-Nasa'i related it from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from Affan, from Hammad ibn Salamah, [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11661).]] and by way of Hammad ibn Zayd; both of them (Hammad ibn Salamah and Hammad ibn Zayd) narrate from Thabit, with the same, but they abridged its beginning. Imam Abu 'Isa at-Tirmidhi has also excelled in it, for he related it in the tafsir of this surah from Mahmud ibn Ghaylan and Abd ibn Humayd, with the same meaning, both saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the 'Asr, he would whisper, and the whisper, in the view of some of them, is moving his lips as if he were speaking. It was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, when you pray 'Asr, you whisper?" He said: "A prophet among the prophets was impressed by his nation and said: 'Who will stand up for these people?' So Allah revealed to him that he should choose between Me taking vengeance upon them, or Me empowering their enemy over them. They chose vengeance, so He empowered death over them, and seventy thousand of them died in one day." He said: And whenever he narrated this hadith, he would narrate this other hadith as well. He said: There was a king among the kings, and that king had a soothsayer who foretold for him. The soothsayer said: "Look for me a boy who is intelligent, or he said: alert and quick-witted, so that I may teach him this knowledge of mine." Then he mentioned the story in full, and at its end he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench, the fire full of fuel﴾ until: ﴿the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾. He said: As for the boy, he was buried. He said: It is mentioned that he was brought out in the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, with his finger upon his temple, just as he had placed it when he was killed. Then at-Tirmidhi said: Hasan gharib. [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (3340).]]

This narration does not explicitly indicate that the context of this story is from the words of the Prophet ﷺ. Our shaykh, the hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, said: It is possible that it is from the words of Suhayb ar-Rumi, for he had knowledge of the reports of the Christians. And Allah knows best.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar also related this story in the Sirah with a different narration, which contradicts what has preceded. He said: Yazid ibn Ziyad narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and also some people of Najran narrated to me from their own people: The people of Najran were polytheists who worshipped idols. In a village of their villages near Najran (and Najran is the great town to which the people of that region gather) there was a sorcerer who taught the boys of Najran sorcery. When a man named Fayman (they did not give me the name that Ibn Munabbih mentioned; they said: a man who settled there) came and set up a tent between Najran and that village where the sorcerer was, the people of Najran began sending their boys to that sorcerer to learn sorcery. Al-Thamir sent his son Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir with the boys of the people of Najran. Whenever he passed by the occupant of the tent, he was impressed by what he saw of his worship and prayer, so he began to sit with him and listen to him, until he embraced Islam, affirmed the oneness of Allah, and worshipped Him. He began asking him about the laws of Islam, and when he became well-versed in it, he began asking him about the Greatest Name, which he (the man in the tent) knew. But he concealed it from him and said: "O my nephew, you will not bear it; I fear your weakness regarding it." Al-Thamir, the father of Abd Allah, did not think except that his son was going to the sorcerer as the boys do. When Abd Allah saw that his companion was withholding it from him and feared his weakness in regard to it, he went and gathered some arrows, then wrote on an arrow every name that he knew of Allah, one name on each arrow. When he had counted them, he lit a fire and began throwing them into it, one arrow after another. When he came to the Greatest Name, he threw his arrow in, and it leapt up and came out of the fire, unharmed by anything. He took it and brought it to his companion and informed him that he had learned the Greatest Name, which the man had concealed from him. He said: "What is it?" He said: "It is such and such." He said: "How did you learn it?" So he told him what he had done. He said: "O my nephew, you have indeed attained it, so keep it to yourself, and I do not think you will do so."

Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir, whenever he entered Najran and met anyone afflicted with harm, would say: "O servant of Allah, will you affirm the oneness of Allah, enter into my religion, and I will supplicate to Allah for you, so that He may relieve you from what you are suffering of affliction?" The person would say: "Yes." He would affirm the oneness of Allah and submit, and he would supplicate to Allah for him, and he would be healed. Until no one in Najran remained who was afflicted with harm without coming to him. They followed him in his affair, and he supplicated for them and they were healed, until his affair reached the king of Najran. He summoned him and said to him: "You have corrupted the people of my town, and you have opposed my religion and the religion of my forefathers. I will surely mutilate you." He said: "You cannot do that." So he began sending him to a long mountain, where he would be thrown from its top, and he would fall to the ground with no harm to him. He also sent him to the waters of Najran, deep seas into which nothing thrown would survive, and he would be cast into them and come out without any harm. When the king became powerless against him, Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir said to him: "You, by Allah, will not be able to kill me until you affirm the oneness of Allah and believe in what I have believed in. For if you do so, you will be empowered over me and kill me." So that king affirmed the oneness of Allah and testified to the testimony of Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir. Then he struck him with a staff in his hand, causing a wound that was not severe, and he died. The king died at that very moment. The people of Najran united upon the religion of Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir, which was what Jesus son of Mary, upon him be peace, had brought, from the Gospel and its law. Then the people were afflicted by what afflicted the people of their religion of innovations, and from there came the origin of the Christian religion in Najran.

Ibn Ishaq said: This is the narration of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and some people of Najran, from Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir, and Allah knows best which of these is correct.

He said: Then Dhu Nuwas marched against them with his army, invited them to Judaism, and gave them the choice between that or death. They chose death, so he dug the trench, burned them with fire, killed them by the sword, and mutilated them, until he had killed nearly twenty thousand of them. Concerning Dhu Nuwas and his army, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench, the fire full of fuel, when they were sitting around it, and they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Witness over all things.﴾ [[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/34).]]

Thus did Muhammad ibn Ishaq mention in the Sirah that the one who killed the People of the Ditch (Ashab al-Ukhdud) was Dhu Nuwas. His name was Zur'ah, and during the time of his kingdom he was called Yusuf. He was the son of Tiban As'ad Abi Karib, and he was the Tubba' who attacked Madinah and covered (kasa) the Ka'bah. He took with him two rabbis from the Jews of Madinah, and through their hands the Jewish faith spread among the people of Yemen, as Ibn Ishaq related in detail. Dhu Nuwas killed twenty thousand people in the Ukhdud in a single morning, and none of them escaped except one man called Daws Dhu Tha'laban, who fled on horseback. They pursued him but could not catch him, so he went to Caesar, king of Syria, who wrote to the Negus, king of Abyssinia. He sent with him an army of Abyssinian Christians led by Aryat and Abrahah, and they rescued Yemen from the hands of the Jews. Dhu Nuwas fled, plunged into the sea, and drowned. The rule of Abyssinia remained in the hands of the Christians for seventy years. Then Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan al-Himyari rescued it from the hands of the Christians, after he sought help from Khosrow, king of Persia, who sent with him those in the prisons, who numbered about seven hundred. With them he conquered Yemen, and rule returned to Himyar. We will, God willing, mention a portion of this in the commentary on the surah: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾

Ibn Ishaq said: I was told by Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm that it was related that a man from the people of Najran, in the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, dug in a ruin of Najran for some need he had, and found Abdullah ibn al-Thamir seated in a grave there, with his hand placed on a wound in his head, holding it with his hand. When they removed his hand from it, blood gushed out, and when they let his hand go, it returned to the wound and stopped the blood. On his hand was a ring on which was written: "My Lord is Allah." They wrote to Umar ibn al-Khattab informing him of the matter, and Umar wrote back to them: "Leave him in his state and return to him the grave in which he was." And they did so. [Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah li-Ibn Hisham (1/36).]

Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Dunya, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abu Bilal al-Ash'ari related to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad related to us, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, who said: some of the people of knowledge told me that when Abu Musa conquered Isfahan, he found a wall of the walls of the city had collapsed. He rebuilt it, and it collapsed; he rebuilt it again, and it collapsed. It was said to him: "Beneath it is a righteous man." So he dug the foundation and found in it a man standing with a sword on which was written: "I am al-Harith ibn Mudad, I condemned the People of the Ditch." Abu Musa brought him out, rebuilt the wall, and it stood firm.

I say: He is al-Harith ibn Mudad ibn Amr ibn Mudad ibn Amr al-Jurhumi, one of the kings of Jurhum who held charge of the Ka'bah after the descendants of Nabt (in another manuscript: "Thabit") ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim. The son of this al-Harith is Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Mudad, the last of the kings of Jurhum in Makkah, when Khuza'ah expelled them and drove them out to Yemen. He is the one who said in the poem which Ibn Hisham said was the first poetry the Arabs composed:

"As if there had never been between al-Hajun and al-Safa a companion, and no one had chatted in Makkah by night.
Indeed, we were its people, but the turns of the nights and the ill-omened fortunes destroyed us."

This indicates that this story was long ago, after the time of Isma'il, peace be upon him, by about five hundred years or so. What Ibn Ishaq mentioned indicates that their story was in the period of interruption (fatrah) between Jesus and Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon them both, and this is more likely, and Allah knows best.

It is possible that such events occurred many times in the world, as Ibn Abi Hatim said:

My father related to us, Abu al-Yaman related to us, Safwan informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, who said: The Ukhdud in Yemen was in the time of Tubba', and in Constantinople in the time of Constantine, when the Christians turned their qibla away from the religion of the Messiah and monotheism. They made a furnace (atun), and the Christians who held to the religion of the Messiah and monotheism were thrown into it. And in Iraq, in the land of Babylon, there was Nebuchadnezzar, who set up the idol and commanded the people to prostrate to it. Daniel and his two companions, Azariah and Mishael, refused, so he kindled for them a furnace, put wood and fire into it, then threw them into it. Allah made it cool and safe for them, and rescued them from it, and He cast into it those who had transgressed against him, who were nine men, and the fire consumed them.

Asbat related from al-Suddi, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿Killed were the companions of the ditch﴾, that he said: The Ukhdud were three: a ditch in Iraq, a ditch in Syria, and a ditch in Yemen. Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

And from Muqatil, who said: The Ukhdud were three: one in Najran in Yemen, another in Syria, and another in Persia. As for the one in Syria, it was Antanunus the Roman; as for the one in Persia, it was Bukhtnassar; and as for the one in the land of the Arabs, it was Yusuf Dhu Nuwas. Regarding those in Persia and Syria, Allah did not send down any Qur'an, but He revealed concerning the one that was in Najran.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dashtaki related to us, Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿Killed were the companions of the ditch﴾, he said: We have heard that they were a people in the period of interruption (fatrah). When they saw the trial and evil that had befallen the people and that they had become factions, ﴿each faction rejoicing in what they have﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 53; al-Rum: 32], they withdrew to a village they settled in, and they remained devoted to the worship of Allah, ﴿sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and establishing prayer and giving zakah﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5]. This was their condition until a tyrant among the tyrants heard of them and was told their story. He sent for them and commanded them to worship the idols they had made, but they all refused and said: "We worship none but Allah alone, with no partner." He said to them: "If you do not worship these gods which I worship, I will kill you." They refused him, so he dug a trench of fire and stood them beside it, and the tyrant said to them: "Choose this, or what we are in." They said: "This is more beloved to us." Among them were women and children, and the children were frightened, so they said to them: "There is no fire after today." They threw themselves into it, and their souls were taken before the heat touched them, and the fire came out from its place and surrounded the tyrants, and Allah burned them with it. Concerning that, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Killed were the companions of the ditch, of the fire full of fuel, when they were sitting over it, and they were witnesses to what they did to the believers. And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is, over all things, Witness﴾.

Ibn Jarir related it: I was told from Ammar, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far, with similar wording [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/88)].

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, those who have tormented the believing men and believing women﴾: that is, burned them. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Abza.

﴿Then they did not repent﴾: that is, they did not desist from what they had done and did not regret what they had committed.

﴿Then for them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the Burning﴾. That is because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Look at this generosity and bounty! They killed His friends, and He calls them to repentance and forgiveness.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 85, verse 1–10 (part 1 of 3):

Tafsir of Surat al-Buruj (The Constellations)
It is a Meccan surah.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Ruzayq ibn Abi Salma narrated to us, Abu al-Muhazzim narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite in the late evening prayer (al-'Isha' al-Akhirah) "By the sky with constellations" (al-Buruj) and "By the sky and the Night-Comer" (al-Tariq) [[al-Musnad (2/326).]].

And Ahmad said: Abu Sa'id, client of the Banu Hashim [[In M: "client of Ibn Hashim".]], narrated to us, Hammad ibn Abbad al-Sadusi narrated to us, I heard Abu al-Muhazzim narrating from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was commanded to recite "by the heavens" in the 'Isha'. [[al-Musnad (2/327).]] Ahmad alone related it.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

Allah swears by the sky and its constellations (buruj), and they are the great stars, as already explained in His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations and placed therein a lamp and a moon giving light﴾ [al-Furqan: 61].

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: "The buruj are the stars." It is also reported from Mujahid: "The buruj are those in which there are guards."

Yahya ibn Rafi' said: "The buruj are palaces in the sky." Al-Minhal ibn Amr said regarding ﴿By the sky with constellations﴾: "It is the good creation."

Ibn Jarir chose that they are the stations of the sun and the moon. They are twelve constellations; the sun travels through each one for a month, and the moon travels through each one for two and a third days, so that makes twenty-eight stations, and it hides for two nights.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿By the promised Day, and the witness and the witnessed﴾, the exegetes differed regarding this. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Amr al-Ghuzzi narrated to us, Ubayd Allah—i.e., Ibn Musa—narrated to us, Musa ibn Ubaydah narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Khalid ibn Safwan ibn AwS al-Ansari, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿By the promised Day﴾ is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and witness﴾ is the Day of Friday. The sun has never risen nor set upon a day better than the Day of Friday. In it there is an hour in which no Muslim servant happens upon it while asking Allah for good except that He gives it to him, and he does not seek refuge in it from evil except that He protects him from it. ﴿And witnessed﴾ is the Day of 'Arafah." [[It was related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (3339), through the route of Rawh ibn Ubadah and Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Musa ibn Ubaydah with the same meaning. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith, which we only know from the hadith of Musa ibn Ubaydah, and Musa ibn Ubaydah is weak in hadith; Yahya ibn Sa'id and others declared him weak."]].

Similarly, Ibn Khuzaymah related this hadith through several routes from Musa ibn Ubaydah al-Rabadhi, who is weak in hadith, and it has been related as a mawquf (halted) report upon Abu Hurayrah, and this is more likely.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, I heard Ali ibn Zayd and Yunus ibn Ubayd narrating from Ammar, client of the Banu Hashim, from Abu Hurayrah—as for Ali, he raised it to the Prophet (ﷺ), and as for Yunus, he did not go beyond Abu Hurayrah—that he said regarding this verse: ﴿And witness and witnessed﴾: He said: "The witness is the Day of Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection." [[al-Musnad (2/298). In it occurs: "The witness is the Day of 'Arafah, and the promised is the Day of Resurrection."]].

Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us from Yunus, I heard Ammar, client of the Banu Hashim, narrating from Abu Hurayrah, and that he said regarding this verse: ﴿And witness and witnessed﴾: He said: "The witness is the Day of Friday, the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafah, and the promised is the Day of Resurrection." [[al-Musnad (2/298, 299).]].

It has also been reported from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "The promised Day is the Day of Resurrection." Likewise al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said so. I have not seen them differ on this, and to Allah belongs all praise.

Then Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Awf narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Damdam ibn Zur'ah narrated to us, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The promised Day is the Day of Resurrection, the witness is the Day of Friday, the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafah, and the Day of Friday Allah has stored up for us." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/82). Al-Tabarani related it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/298) from Hashim ibn Murthid, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il with it, and in it there is weakness and a break in the chain; this chain has been mentioned many times before.]].

Then Ibn Jarir said: Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to us, Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, from Ibn Harmalah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the master of days is the Day of Friday, and it is the witness, and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafah." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/82).]].

This is a mursal report from the mursal reports of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. Then Ibn Jarir said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf al-Makki, from Ibn Abbas who said: "The witness is Muhammad (ﷺ), and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection," then he recited: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed﴾ [Hud: 103]. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/83).]]

And Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Shibak who said: A man asked al-Hasan ibn Ali about ﴿And witness and witnessed﴾. He said: "Did you ask anyone before me?" He said: "Yes, I asked Ibn Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr, and they said: the Day of Sacrifice and the Day of Friday." He said: "No, but the witness is Muhammad (ﷺ)," then he recited: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you against these as a witness﴾ [al-Nisa: 41], "and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection," then he recited: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed﴾. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/83).]]

This is also what al-Hasan al-Basri said. Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Ibn Harmalah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: "﴿And witnessed﴾ is the Day of Resurrection."

Mujahid, Ikrimah and al-Dahhak said: "The witness is the son of Adam, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."

Also from Ikrimah: "The witness is Muhammad (ﷺ), and the witnessed is the Day of Friday."

[Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: "The witness is Allah, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."] [[Addition from M, A, and al-Tabari.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Yahya al-Qattat, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And witness and witnessed﴾: He said: "The witness is the human being, and the witnessed is the Day of Friday." Thus Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And witness and witnessed﴾: "The witness is the Day of 'Arafah, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."

And with the same chain, from Sufyan—he is al-Thawri—from Mughirah, from Ibrahim who said: "The Day of Sacrifice and the Day of 'Arafah," meaning the witness and the witnessed.

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: "The witnessed is the Day of Friday," and they narrated in support of that what Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us: my paternal uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb informed me, Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Zayd ibn Aymam, from Ubadah ibn Nusayy, from Abu al-Darda' who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Increase your sending of blessings upon me on the Day of Friday, for it is a witnessed day, which the angels witness." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/84).]]

And from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "The witness is Allah, and he recited: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾ [al-Nisa: 79], and the witnessed is us." Al-Baghawi related it and said: "Most scholars hold that the witness is the Day of Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafah."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench﴾, meaning: cursed were the companions of the trench. Its plural is akhadid, and it is a pit dug in the earth. This is a report about a people of the disbelievers who targeted the believers in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, among them, overpowered them, and wanted them to turn back from their religion, but they refused. So they dug for them a trench in the earth and kindled fire in it, and prepared fuel with which to stoke it. Then they confronted them, but they would not accept from them, so they threw them into it. This is why Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench, the fire full of fuel, when they sat beside it, and they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers﴾, meaning: they were watching what was being done to those believers.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾, meaning: they had no sin in their eyes except their belief in Allah, the Mighty, who is not wronged by one who seeks refuge in His presence, the Unassailable, the Praiseworthy in all His actions, sayings, legislation and decree. And even if He decreed upon these servants what befell them at the hands of the disbelievers, He is still the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, even if the reason for that is hidden from many people.

Then He said: ﴿To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾: as a complement to the attribute, He is the owner of all the heavens and the earth and what is in them and between them. ﴿And Allah is witness over all things﴾, meaning: nothing in all the heavens and the earth is hidden from Him, and no hidden thing is concealed from Him.

The exegetes differed about who the people of this story were. From Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, it is reported that they were the people of Persia, when their king wanted to make lawful the marrying of close relatives, and their scholars refused him, so he set out to dig a trench and threw into it whoever among them denounced him, and the lawfulness of close marriages continued among them until today.

Also from him: they were a people in Yemen among whom believers and polytheists fought; the believers overcame their disbelievers, then they fought again and the disbelievers overcame the believers, so they dug trenches for them and burned them in them.

Also from him: they were from among the Abyssinians, and their one [i.e., their prophet] was an Abyssinian.

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench, the fire full of fuel﴾: He said: "People from the Children of Israel dug a trench in the earth, then kindled a fire in it, then they stood over that trench with men and women, and they were presented to it. And they claimed that it was Daniel and his companions."

This is also what al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said, and other things have been said. Imam Ahmad said:

Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There was a king among those before you, and he had a sorcerer. When the sorcerer grew old, he said to the king: 'I have grown old and my appointed time has come, so send me a boy to teach him sorcery.' So he sent him a boy, and he taught him sorcery. Between the sorcerer and the king there was a monk, so the boy came upon the monk and heard his speech, and he was pleased with his manner and his speech. Whenever he came to the sorcerer, he would strike him and say: 'What delayed you?' And whenever he came to his family, they would strike him and say: 'What delayed you?' So he complained of that to the monk, who said: 'When the sorcerer wants to strike you, say: "My family detained me." And when your family want to strike you, say: "The sorcerer detained me."

He said: One day, while he was passing by, he came upon a huge, terrifying creature that had blocked the people, so that they could not pass. He said: "Today I will know whether the matter of the monk is more beloved to Allah, or the matter of the sorcerer." He then took a stone and said: "O Allah, if the matter of the monk is more beloved to You and more pleasing to You than the matter of the sorcerer, then kill this creature so that the people may pass." He threw it and killed it, and the people passed on. The monk was informed of this and said: "My son, you are better than me, and you will be tested. If you are tested, do not point to me." The boy used to heal the blind, the leper, and all other diseases, and cure them. A companion of the king had gone blind, so he heard about him and came to him with many gifts, saying: "Cure me, and all of this here will be yours." He replied: "I do not cure anyone. Only Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cures. If you believe in Him, I will supplicate to Allah, and He will cure you." He believed, supplicated to Allah, and Allah cured him. Then he went to the king and sat in his usual place. The king said to him: "O so-and-so, who restored your sight?" He said: "My Lord." He said: "Me?" He said: "No, my Lord and your Lord is Allah." He said: "Do you have a lord other than me?" He said: "Yes, my Lord and your Lord is Allah." He kept torturing him until he pointed to the boy. He sent for the boy and said: "My son, has your sorcery reached the point where you can cure the blind, the leper, and these diseases?" He said: "I do not cure anyone. Only Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cures." He said: "Me?" He said: "No." He said: "Do you have a lord other than me?" He said: "My Lord and your Lord is Allah." So he tortured him also, until he pointed to the monk. The monk was brought, and the king said: "Turn back from your religion." He refused, so he placed the saw at the middle of his head until his two halves fell apart. Then he said to the blind man: "Turn back from your religion." He refused, so he placed the saw at the middle of his head until his two halves fell to the ground. He said to the boy: "Turn back from your religion." He refused, so he sent him with a group of men to such-and-such mountain, saying: "When you reach its peak, if he turns back from his religion, (good); otherwise, throw him down [from above]." [[Addition from the Musnad.]] They took him away, and when they reached the top of the mountain, he said: "O Allah, suffice me against them however You wish." The mountain shook under them, and they all were thrown down. The boy came walking until he entered upon the king and said: "What did your companions do?" He said: "Allah has sufficed me against them." So the king sent him with a group in a small boat, saying: "When you take him out into the middle of the sea, if he turns back from his religion, (good); otherwise, drown him in the sea." They took him out into the middle of the sea, and the boy said: "O Allah, suffice me against them however You wish." They all drowned, and the boy came until he entered upon the king and said: "What did your companions do?" He said: "Allah has sufficed me against them." Then he said to the king: "You will not kill me until you do what I command you. If you do what I command you, you will kill me; otherwise, you will not be able to kill me." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "Gather the people in one open place, then crucify me on a trunk, take an arrow from my quiver, and say: 'In the name of Allah, Lord of the boy.' For when you do that, you will kill me." He did so, placed the arrow in the middle of his bow, threw it, and said: "In the name of Allah, Lord of the boy." The arrow struck his temple, and the boy placed his hand on the spot where the arrow had struck and died. The people said: "We believe in the Lord of the boy." It was said to the king: "Have you seen what you were fearing? By Allah, it has come upon you. All the people have believed." So he ordered that trenches be dug at the mouths of the alleys, the trenches were dug, fires were kindled in them, and he said: "Whoever turns back from his religion, let him go; otherwise, throw him into them." He said: "They were pushing and shoving one another into them. Then a woman came with a son of hers whom she was nursing, and it seemed she hesitated to fall into the fire. The child said: 'Be patient, O mother, for you are upon the truth.'"

This is how Muslim related it at the end of his Sahih, from Hudbah ibn Khalid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with similar wording. [[Musnad (6/16) and Sahih Muslim, no. (3005).]] An-Nasa'i related it from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from Affan, from Hammad ibn Salamah, [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11661).]] and by way of Hammad ibn Zayd; both of them (Hammad ibn Salamah and Hammad ibn Zayd) narrate from Thabit, with the same, but they abridged its beginning. Imam Abu 'Isa at-Tirmidhi has also excelled in it, for he related it in the tafsir of this surah from Mahmud ibn Ghaylan and Abd ibn Humayd, with the same meaning, both saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the 'Asr, he would whisper, and the whisper, in the view of some of them, is moving his lips as if he were speaking. It was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, when you pray 'Asr, you whisper?" He said: "A prophet among the prophets was impressed by his nation and said: 'Who will stand up for these people?' So Allah revealed to him that he should choose between Me taking vengeance upon them, or Me empowering their enemy over them. They chose vengeance, so He empowered death over them, and seventy thousand of them died in one day." He said: And whenever he narrated this hadith, he would narrate this other hadith as well. He said: There was a king among the kings, and that king had a soothsayer who foretold for him. The soothsayer said: "Look for me a boy who is intelligent, or he said: alert and quick-witted, so that I may teach him this knowledge of mine." Then he mentioned the story in full, and at its end he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench, the fire full of fuel﴾ until: ﴿the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾. He said: As for the boy, he was buried. He said: It is mentioned that he was brought out in the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, with his finger upon his temple, just as he had placed it when he was killed. Then at-Tirmidhi said: Hasan gharib. [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (3340).]]

This narration does not explicitly indicate that the context of this story is from the words of the Prophet ﷺ. Our shaykh, the hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, said: It is possible that it is from the words of Suhayb ar-Rumi, for he had knowledge of the reports of the Christians. And Allah knows best.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar also related this story in the Sirah with a different narration, which contradicts what has preceded. He said: Yazid ibn Ziyad narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and also some people of Najran narrated to me from their own people: The people of Najran were polytheists who worshipped idols. In a village of their villages near Najran (and Najran is the great town to which the people of that region gather) there was a sorcerer who taught the boys of Najran sorcery. When a man named Fayman (they did not give me the name that Ibn Munabbih mentioned; they said: a man who settled there) came and set up a tent between Najran and that village where the sorcerer was, the people of Najran began sending their boys to that sorcerer to learn sorcery. Al-Thamir sent his son Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir with the boys of the people of Najran. Whenever he passed by the occupant of the tent, he was impressed by what he saw of his worship and prayer, so he began to sit with him and listen to him, until he embraced Islam, affirmed the oneness of Allah, and worshipped Him. He began asking him about the laws of Islam, and when he became well-versed in it, he began asking him about the Greatest Name, which he (the man in the tent) knew. But he concealed it from him and said: "O my nephew, you will not bear it; I fear your weakness regarding it." Al-Thamir, the father of Abd Allah, did not think except that his son was going to the sorcerer as the boys do. When Abd Allah saw that his companion was withholding it from him and feared his weakness in regard to it, he went and gathered some arrows, then wrote on an arrow every name that he knew of Allah, one name on each arrow. When he had counted them, he lit a fire and began throwing them into it, one arrow after another. When he came to the Greatest Name, he threw his arrow in, and it leapt up and came out of the fire, unharmed by anything. He took it and brought it to his companion and informed him that he had learned the Greatest Name, which the man had concealed from him. He said: "What is it?" He said: "It is such and such." He said: "How did you learn it?" So he told him what he had done. He said: "O my nephew, you have indeed attained it, so keep it to yourself, and I do not think you will do so."

Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir, whenever he entered Najran and met anyone afflicted with harm, would say: "O servant of Allah, will you affirm the oneness of Allah, enter into my religion, and I will supplicate to Allah for you, so that He may relieve you from what you are suffering of affliction?" The person would say: "Yes." He would affirm the oneness of Allah and submit, and he would supplicate to Allah for him, and he would be healed. Until no one in Najran remained who was afflicted with harm without coming to him. They followed him in his affair, and he supplicated for them and they were healed, until his affair reached the king of Najran. He summoned him and said to him: "You have corrupted the people of my town, and you have opposed my religion and the religion of my forefathers. I will surely mutilate you." He said: "You cannot do that." So he began sending him to a long mountain, where he would be thrown from its top, and he would fall to the ground with no harm to him. He also sent him to the waters of Najran, deep seas into which nothing thrown would survive, and he would be cast into them and come out without any harm. When the king became powerless against him, Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir said to him: "You, by Allah, will not be able to kill me until you affirm the oneness of Allah and believe in what I have believed in. For if you do so, you will be empowered over me and kill me." So that king affirmed the oneness of Allah and testified to the testimony of Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir. Then he struck him with a staff in his hand, causing a wound that was not severe, and he died. The king died at that very moment. The people of Najran united upon the religion of Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir, which was what Jesus son of Mary, upon him be peace, had brought, from the Gospel and its law. Then the people were afflicted by what afflicted the people of their religion of innovations, and from there came the origin of the Christian religion in Najran.

Ibn Ishaq said: This is the narration of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and some people of Najran, from Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir, and Allah knows best which of these is correct.

He said: Then Dhu Nuwas marched against them with his army, invited them to Judaism, and gave them the choice between that or death. They chose death, so he dug the trench, burned them with fire, killed them by the sword, and mutilated them, until he had killed nearly twenty thousand of them. Concerning Dhu Nuwas and his army, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench, the fire full of fuel, when they were sitting around it, and they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Witness over all things.﴾ [[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/34).]]

Thus did Muhammad ibn Ishaq mention in the Sirah that the one who killed the People of the Ditch (Ashab al-Ukhdud) was Dhu Nuwas. His name was Zur'ah, and during the time of his kingdom he was called Yusuf. He was the son of Tiban As'ad Abi Karib, and he was the Tubba' who attacked Madinah and covered (kasa) the Ka'bah. He took with him two rabbis from the Jews of Madinah, and through their hands the Jewish faith spread among the people of Yemen, as Ibn Ishaq related in detail. Dhu Nuwas killed twenty thousand people in the Ukhdud in a single morning, and none of them escaped except one man called Daws Dhu Tha'laban, who fled on horseback. They pursued him but could not catch him, so he went to Caesar, king of Syria, who wrote to the Negus, king of Abyssinia. He sent with him an army of Abyssinian Christians led by Aryat and Abrahah, and they rescued Yemen from the hands of the Jews. Dhu Nuwas fled, plunged into the sea, and drowned. The rule of Abyssinia remained in the hands of the Christians for seventy years. Then Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan al-Himyari rescued it from the hands of the Christians, after he sought help from Khosrow, king of Persia, who sent with him those in the prisons, who numbered about seven hundred. With them he conquered Yemen, and rule returned to Himyar. We will, God willing, mention a portion of this in the commentary on the surah: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾

Ibn Ishaq said: I was told by Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm that it was related that a man from the people of Najran, in the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, dug in a ruin of Najran for some need he had, and found Abdullah ibn al-Thamir seated in a grave there, with his hand placed on a wound in his head, holding it with his hand. When they removed his hand from it, blood gushed out, and when they let his hand go, it returned to the wound and stopped the blood. On his hand was a ring on which was written: "My Lord is Allah." They wrote to Umar ibn al-Khattab informing him of the matter, and Umar wrote back to them: "Leave him in his state and return to him the grave in which he was." And they did so. [Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah li-Ibn Hisham (1/36).]

Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Dunya, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abu Bilal al-Ash'ari related to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad related to us, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, who said: some of the people of knowledge told me that when Abu Musa conquered Isfahan, he found a wall of the walls of the city had collapsed. He rebuilt it, and it collapsed; he rebuilt it again, and it collapsed. It was said to him: "Beneath it is a righteous man." So he dug the foundation and found in it a man standing with a sword on which was written: "I am al-Harith ibn Mudad, I condemned the People of the Ditch." Abu Musa brought him out, rebuilt the wall, and it stood firm.

I say: He is al-Harith ibn Mudad ibn Amr ibn Mudad ibn Amr al-Jurhumi, one of the kings of Jurhum who held charge of the Ka'bah after the descendants of Nabt (in another manuscript: "Thabit") ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim. The son of this al-Harith is Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Mudad, the last of the kings of Jurhum in Makkah, when Khuza'ah expelled them and drove them out to Yemen. He is the one who said in the poem which Ibn Hisham said was the first poetry the Arabs composed:

"As if there had never been between al-Hajun and al-Safa a companion, and no one had chatted in Makkah by night.
Indeed, we were its people, but the turns of the nights and the ill-omened fortunes destroyed us."

This indicates that this story was long ago, after the time of Isma'il, peace be upon him, by about five hundred years or so. What Ibn Ishaq mentioned indicates that their story was in the period of interruption (fatrah) between Jesus and Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon them both, and this is more likely, and Allah knows best.

It is possible that such events occurred many times in the world, as Ibn Abi Hatim said:

My father related to us, Abu al-Yaman related to us, Safwan informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, who said: The Ukhdud in Yemen was in the time of Tubba', and in Constantinople in the time of Constantine, when the Christians turned their qibla away from the religion of the Messiah and monotheism. They made a furnace (atun), and the Christians who held to the religion of the Messiah and monotheism were thrown into it. And in Iraq, in the land of Babylon, there was Nebuchadnezzar, who set up the idol and commanded the people to prostrate to it. Daniel and his two companions, Azariah and Mishael, refused, so he kindled for them a furnace, put wood and fire into it, then threw them into it. Allah made it cool and safe for them, and rescued them from it, and He cast into it those who had transgressed against him, who were nine men, and the fire consumed them.

Asbat related from al-Suddi, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿Killed were the companions of the ditch﴾, that he said: The Ukhdud were three: a ditch in Iraq, a ditch in Syria, and a ditch in Yemen. Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

And from Muqatil, who said: The Ukhdud were three: one in Najran in Yemen, another in Syria, and another in Persia. As for the one in Syria, it was Antanunus the Roman; as for the one in Persia, it was Bukhtnassar; and as for the one in the land of the Arabs, it was Yusuf Dhu Nuwas. Regarding those in Persia and Syria, Allah did not send down any Qur'an, but He revealed concerning the one that was in Najran.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dashtaki related to us, Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿Killed were the companions of the ditch﴾, he said: We have heard that they were a people in the period of interruption (fatrah). When they saw the trial and evil that had befallen the people and that they had become factions, ﴿each faction rejoicing in what they have﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 53; al-Rum: 32], they withdrew to a village they settled in, and they remained devoted to the worship of Allah, ﴿sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and establishing prayer and giving zakah﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5]. This was their condition until a tyrant among the tyrants heard of them and was told their story. He sent for them and commanded them to worship the idols they had made, but they all refused and said: "We worship none but Allah alone, with no partner." He said to them: "If you do not worship these gods which I worship, I will kill you." They refused him, so he dug a trench of fire and stood them beside it, and the tyrant said to them: "Choose this, or what we are in." They said: "This is more beloved to us." Among them were women and children, and the children were frightened, so they said to them: "There is no fire after today." They threw themselves into it, and their souls were taken before the heat touched them, and the fire came out from its place and surrounded the tyrants, and Allah burned them with it. Concerning that, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Killed were the companions of the ditch, of the fire full of fuel, when they were sitting over it, and they were witnesses to what they did to the believers. And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is, over all things, Witness﴾.

Ibn Jarir related it: I was told from Ammar, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far, with similar wording [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/88)].

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, those who have tormented the believing men and believing women﴾: that is, burned them. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Abza.

﴿Then they did not repent﴾: that is, they did not desist from what they had done and did not regret what they had committed.

﴿Then for them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the Burning﴾. That is because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Look at this generosity and bounty! They killed His friends, and He calls them to repentance and forgiveness.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 85, verse 1–10 (part 1 of 3):

Tafsir of Surat al-Buruj (The Constellations)
It is a Meccan surah.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Ruzayq ibn Abi Salma narrated to us, Abu al-Muhazzim narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite in the late evening prayer (al-'Isha' al-Akhirah) "By the sky with constellations" (al-Buruj) and "By the sky and the Night-Comer" (al-Tariq) [[al-Musnad (2/326).]].

And Ahmad said: Abu Sa'id, client of the Banu Hashim [[In M: "client of Ibn Hashim".]], narrated to us, Hammad ibn Abbad al-Sadusi narrated to us, I heard Abu al-Muhazzim narrating from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was commanded to recite "by the heavens" in the 'Isha'. [[al-Musnad (2/327).]] Ahmad alone related it.

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

Allah swears by the sky and its constellations (buruj), and they are the great stars, as already explained in His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations and placed therein a lamp and a moon giving light﴾ [al-Furqan: 61].

Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: "The buruj are the stars." It is also reported from Mujahid: "The buruj are those in which there are guards."

Yahya ibn Rafi' said: "The buruj are palaces in the sky." Al-Minhal ibn Amr said regarding ﴿By the sky with constellations﴾: "It is the good creation."

Ibn Jarir chose that they are the stations of the sun and the moon. They are twelve constellations; the sun travels through each one for a month, and the moon travels through each one for two and a third days, so that makes twenty-eight stations, and it hides for two nights.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿By the promised Day, and the witness and the witnessed﴾, the exegetes differed regarding this. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Amr al-Ghuzzi narrated to us, Ubayd Allah—i.e., Ibn Musa—narrated to us, Musa ibn Ubaydah narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Khalid ibn Safwan ibn AwS al-Ansari, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿By the promised Day﴾ is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and witness﴾ is the Day of Friday. The sun has never risen nor set upon a day better than the Day of Friday. In it there is an hour in which no Muslim servant happens upon it while asking Allah for good except that He gives it to him, and he does not seek refuge in it from evil except that He protects him from it. ﴿And witnessed﴾ is the Day of 'Arafah." [[It was related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (3339), through the route of Rawh ibn Ubadah and Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Musa ibn Ubaydah with the same meaning. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith, which we only know from the hadith of Musa ibn Ubaydah, and Musa ibn Ubaydah is weak in hadith; Yahya ibn Sa'id and others declared him weak."]].

Similarly, Ibn Khuzaymah related this hadith through several routes from Musa ibn Ubaydah al-Rabadhi, who is weak in hadith, and it has been related as a mawquf (halted) report upon Abu Hurayrah, and this is more likely.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, I heard Ali ibn Zayd and Yunus ibn Ubayd narrating from Ammar, client of the Banu Hashim, from Abu Hurayrah—as for Ali, he raised it to the Prophet (ﷺ), and as for Yunus, he did not go beyond Abu Hurayrah—that he said regarding this verse: ﴿And witness and witnessed﴾: He said: "The witness is the Day of Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection." [[al-Musnad (2/298). In it occurs: "The witness is the Day of 'Arafah, and the promised is the Day of Resurrection."]].

Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us from Yunus, I heard Ammar, client of the Banu Hashim, narrating from Abu Hurayrah, and that he said regarding this verse: ﴿And witness and witnessed﴾: He said: "The witness is the Day of Friday, the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafah, and the promised is the Day of Resurrection." [[al-Musnad (2/298, 299).]].

It has also been reported from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "The promised Day is the Day of Resurrection." Likewise al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said so. I have not seen them differ on this, and to Allah belongs all praise.

Then Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Awf narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ayyash narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Damdam ibn Zur'ah narrated to us, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The promised Day is the Day of Resurrection, the witness is the Day of Friday, the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafah, and the Day of Friday Allah has stored up for us." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/82). Al-Tabarani related it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/298) from Hashim ibn Murthid, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il with it, and in it there is weakness and a break in the chain; this chain has been mentioned many times before.]].

Then Ibn Jarir said: Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to us, Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, from Ibn Harmalah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the master of days is the Day of Friday, and it is the witness, and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafah." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/82).]].

This is a mursal report from the mursal reports of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. Then Ibn Jarir said:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf al-Makki, from Ibn Abbas who said: "The witness is Muhammad (ﷺ), and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection," then he recited: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed﴾ [Hud: 103]. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/83).]]

And Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Shibak who said: A man asked al-Hasan ibn Ali about ﴿And witness and witnessed﴾. He said: "Did you ask anyone before me?" He said: "Yes, I asked Ibn Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr, and they said: the Day of Sacrifice and the Day of Friday." He said: "No, but the witness is Muhammad (ﷺ)," then he recited: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you against these as a witness﴾ [al-Nisa: 41], "and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection," then he recited: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed﴾. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/83).]]

This is also what al-Hasan al-Basri said. Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Ibn Harmalah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: "﴿And witnessed﴾ is the Day of Resurrection."

Mujahid, Ikrimah and al-Dahhak said: "The witness is the son of Adam, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."

Also from Ikrimah: "The witness is Muhammad (ﷺ), and the witnessed is the Day of Friday."

[Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: "The witness is Allah, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."] [[Addition from M, A, and al-Tabari.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Nu'aym al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Yahya al-Qattat, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And witness and witnessed﴾: He said: "The witness is the human being, and the witnessed is the Day of Friday." Thus Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And witness and witnessed﴾: "The witness is the Day of 'Arafah, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection."

And with the same chain, from Sufyan—he is al-Thawri—from Mughirah, from Ibrahim who said: "The Day of Sacrifice and the Day of 'Arafah," meaning the witness and the witnessed.

Ibn Jarir said: Others said: "The witnessed is the Day of Friday," and they narrated in support of that what Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us: my paternal uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb informed me, Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Zayd ibn Aymam, from Ubadah ibn Nusayy, from Abu al-Darda' who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Increase your sending of blessings upon me on the Day of Friday, for it is a witnessed day, which the angels witness." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/84).]]

And from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "The witness is Allah, and he recited: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾ [al-Nisa: 79], and the witnessed is us." Al-Baghawi related it and said: "Most scholars hold that the witness is the Day of Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafah."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench﴾, meaning: cursed were the companions of the trench. Its plural is akhadid, and it is a pit dug in the earth. This is a report about a people of the disbelievers who targeted the believers in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, among them, overpowered them, and wanted them to turn back from their religion, but they refused. So they dug for them a trench in the earth and kindled fire in it, and prepared fuel with which to stoke it. Then they confronted them, but they would not accept from them, so they threw them into it. This is why Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench, the fire full of fuel, when they sat beside it, and they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers﴾, meaning: they were watching what was being done to those believers.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾, meaning: they had no sin in their eyes except their belief in Allah, the Mighty, who is not wronged by one who seeks refuge in His presence, the Unassailable, the Praiseworthy in all His actions, sayings, legislation and decree. And even if He decreed upon these servants what befell them at the hands of the disbelievers, He is still the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, even if the reason for that is hidden from many people.

Then He said: ﴿To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾: as a complement to the attribute, He is the owner of all the heavens and the earth and what is in them and between them. ﴿And Allah is witness over all things﴾, meaning: nothing in all the heavens and the earth is hidden from Him, and no hidden thing is concealed from Him.

The exegetes differed about who the people of this story were. From Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, it is reported that they were the people of Persia, when their king wanted to make lawful the marrying of close relatives, and their scholars refused him, so he set out to dig a trench and threw into it whoever among them denounced him, and the lawfulness of close marriages continued among them until today.

Also from him: they were a people in Yemen among whom believers and polytheists fought; the believers overcame their disbelievers, then they fought again and the disbelievers overcame the believers, so they dug trenches for them and burned them in them.

Also from him: they were from among the Abyssinians, and their one [i.e., their prophet] was an Abyssinian.

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench, the fire full of fuel﴾: He said: "People from the Children of Israel dug a trench in the earth, then kindled a fire in it, then they stood over that trench with men and women, and they were presented to it. And they claimed that it was Daniel and his companions."

This is also what al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said, and other things have been said. Imam Ahmad said:

Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There was a king among those before you, and he had a sorcerer. When the sorcerer grew old, he said to the king: 'I have grown old and my appointed time has come, so send me a boy to teach him sorcery.' So he sent him a boy, and he taught him sorcery. Between the sorcerer and the king there was a monk, so the boy came upon the monk and heard his speech, and he was pleased with his manner and his speech. Whenever he came to the sorcerer, he would strike him and say: 'What delayed you?' And whenever he came to his family, they would strike him and say: 'What delayed you?' So he complained of that to the monk, who said: 'When the sorcerer wants to strike you, say: "My family detained me." And when your family want to strike you, say: "The sorcerer detained me."

He said: One day, while he was passing by, he came upon a huge, terrifying creature that had blocked the people, so that they could not pass. He said: "Today I will know whether the matter of the monk is more beloved to Allah, or the matter of the sorcerer." He then took a stone and said: "O Allah, if the matter of the monk is more beloved to You and more pleasing to You than the matter of the sorcerer, then kill this creature so that the people may pass." He threw it and killed it, and the people passed on. The monk was informed of this and said: "My son, you are better than me, and you will be tested. If you are tested, do not point to me." The boy used to heal the blind, the leper, and all other diseases, and cure them. A companion of the king had gone blind, so he heard about him and came to him with many gifts, saying: "Cure me, and all of this here will be yours." He replied: "I do not cure anyone. Only Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cures. If you believe in Him, I will supplicate to Allah, and He will cure you." He believed, supplicated to Allah, and Allah cured him. Then he went to the king and sat in his usual place. The king said to him: "O so-and-so, who restored your sight?" He said: "My Lord." He said: "Me?" He said: "No, my Lord and your Lord is Allah." He said: "Do you have a lord other than me?" He said: "Yes, my Lord and your Lord is Allah." He kept torturing him until he pointed to the boy. He sent for the boy and said: "My son, has your sorcery reached the point where you can cure the blind, the leper, and these diseases?" He said: "I do not cure anyone. Only Allah, Mighty and Majestic, cures." He said: "Me?" He said: "No." He said: "Do you have a lord other than me?" He said: "My Lord and your Lord is Allah." So he tortured him also, until he pointed to the monk. The monk was brought, and the king said: "Turn back from your religion." He refused, so he placed the saw at the middle of his head until his two halves fell apart. Then he said to the blind man: "Turn back from your religion." He refused, so he placed the saw at the middle of his head until his two halves fell to the ground. He said to the boy: "Turn back from your religion." He refused, so he sent him with a group of men to such-and-such mountain, saying: "When you reach its peak, if he turns back from his religion, (good); otherwise, throw him down [from above]." [[Addition from the Musnad.]] They took him away, and when they reached the top of the mountain, he said: "O Allah, suffice me against them however You wish." The mountain shook under them, and they all were thrown down. The boy came walking until he entered upon the king and said: "What did your companions do?" He said: "Allah has sufficed me against them." So the king sent him with a group in a small boat, saying: "When you take him out into the middle of the sea, if he turns back from his religion, (good); otherwise, drown him in the sea." They took him out into the middle of the sea, and the boy said: "O Allah, suffice me against them however You wish." They all drowned, and the boy came until he entered upon the king and said: "What did your companions do?" He said: "Allah has sufficed me against them." Then he said to the king: "You will not kill me until you do what I command you. If you do what I command you, you will kill me; otherwise, you will not be able to kill me." He said: "And what is it?" He said: "Gather the people in one open place, then crucify me on a trunk, take an arrow from my quiver, and say: 'In the name of Allah, Lord of the boy.' For when you do that, you will kill me." He did so, placed the arrow in the middle of his bow, threw it, and said: "In the name of Allah, Lord of the boy." The arrow struck his temple, and the boy placed his hand on the spot where the arrow had struck and died. The people said: "We believe in the Lord of the boy." It was said to the king: "Have you seen what you were fearing? By Allah, it has come upon you. All the people have believed." So he ordered that trenches be dug at the mouths of the alleys, the trenches were dug, fires were kindled in them, and he said: "Whoever turns back from his religion, let him go; otherwise, throw him into them." He said: "They were pushing and shoving one another into them. Then a woman came with a son of hers whom she was nursing, and it seemed she hesitated to fall into the fire. The child said: 'Be patient, O mother, for you are upon the truth.'"

This is how Muslim related it at the end of his Sahih, from Hudbah ibn Khalid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with similar wording. [[Musnad (6/16) and Sahih Muslim, no. (3005).]] An-Nasa'i related it from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, from Affan, from Hammad ibn Salamah, [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11661).]] and by way of Hammad ibn Zayd; both of them (Hammad ibn Salamah and Hammad ibn Zayd) narrate from Thabit, with the same, but they abridged its beginning. Imam Abu 'Isa at-Tirmidhi has also excelled in it, for he related it in the tafsir of this surah from Mahmud ibn Ghaylan and Abd ibn Humayd, with the same meaning, both saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Suhayb, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the 'Asr, he would whisper, and the whisper, in the view of some of them, is moving his lips as if he were speaking. It was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, when you pray 'Asr, you whisper?" He said: "A prophet among the prophets was impressed by his nation and said: 'Who will stand up for these people?' So Allah revealed to him that he should choose between Me taking vengeance upon them, or Me empowering their enemy over them. They chose vengeance, so He empowered death over them, and seventy thousand of them died in one day." He said: And whenever he narrated this hadith, he would narrate this other hadith as well. He said: There was a king among the kings, and that king had a soothsayer who foretold for him. The soothsayer said: "Look for me a boy who is intelligent, or he said: alert and quick-witted, so that I may teach him this knowledge of mine." Then he mentioned the story in full, and at its end he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench, the fire full of fuel﴾ until: ﴿the Almighty, the Praiseworthy﴾. He said: As for the boy, he was buried. He said: It is mentioned that he was brought out in the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, with his finger upon his temple, just as he had placed it when he was killed. Then at-Tirmidhi said: Hasan gharib. [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. (3340).]]

This narration does not explicitly indicate that the context of this story is from the words of the Prophet ﷺ. Our shaykh, the hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, said: It is possible that it is from the words of Suhayb ar-Rumi, for he had knowledge of the reports of the Christians. And Allah knows best.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar also related this story in the Sirah with a different narration, which contradicts what has preceded. He said: Yazid ibn Ziyad narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and also some people of Najran narrated to me from their own people: The people of Najran were polytheists who worshipped idols. In a village of their villages near Najran (and Najran is the great town to which the people of that region gather) there was a sorcerer who taught the boys of Najran sorcery. When a man named Fayman (they did not give me the name that Ibn Munabbih mentioned; they said: a man who settled there) came and set up a tent between Najran and that village where the sorcerer was, the people of Najran began sending their boys to that sorcerer to learn sorcery. Al-Thamir sent his son Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir with the boys of the people of Najran. Whenever he passed by the occupant of the tent, he was impressed by what he saw of his worship and prayer, so he began to sit with him and listen to him, until he embraced Islam, affirmed the oneness of Allah, and worshipped Him. He began asking him about the laws of Islam, and when he became well-versed in it, he began asking him about the Greatest Name, which he (the man in the tent) knew. But he concealed it from him and said: "O my nephew, you will not bear it; I fear your weakness regarding it." Al-Thamir, the father of Abd Allah, did not think except that his son was going to the sorcerer as the boys do. When Abd Allah saw that his companion was withholding it from him and feared his weakness in regard to it, he went and gathered some arrows, then wrote on an arrow every name that he knew of Allah, one name on each arrow. When he had counted them, he lit a fire and began throwing them into it, one arrow after another. When he came to the Greatest Name, he threw his arrow in, and it leapt up and came out of the fire, unharmed by anything. He took it and brought it to his companion and informed him that he had learned the Greatest Name, which the man had concealed from him. He said: "What is it?" He said: "It is such and such." He said: "How did you learn it?" So he told him what he had done. He said: "O my nephew, you have indeed attained it, so keep it to yourself, and I do not think you will do so."

Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir, whenever he entered Najran and met anyone afflicted with harm, would say: "O servant of Allah, will you affirm the oneness of Allah, enter into my religion, and I will supplicate to Allah for you, so that He may relieve you from what you are suffering of affliction?" The person would say: "Yes." He would affirm the oneness of Allah and submit, and he would supplicate to Allah for him, and he would be healed. Until no one in Najran remained who was afflicted with harm without coming to him. They followed him in his affair, and he supplicated for them and they were healed, until his affair reached the king of Najran. He summoned him and said to him: "You have corrupted the people of my town, and you have opposed my religion and the religion of my forefathers. I will surely mutilate you." He said: "You cannot do that." So he began sending him to a long mountain, where he would be thrown from its top, and he would fall to the ground with no harm to him. He also sent him to the waters of Najran, deep seas into which nothing thrown would survive, and he would be cast into them and come out without any harm. When the king became powerless against him, Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir said to him: "You, by Allah, will not be able to kill me until you affirm the oneness of Allah and believe in what I have believed in. For if you do so, you will be empowered over me and kill me." So that king affirmed the oneness of Allah and testified to the testimony of Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir. Then he struck him with a staff in his hand, causing a wound that was not severe, and he died. The king died at that very moment. The people of Najran united upon the religion of Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir, which was what Jesus son of Mary, upon him be peace, had brought, from the Gospel and its law. Then the people were afflicted by what afflicted the people of their religion of innovations, and from there came the origin of the Christian religion in Najran.

Ibn Ishaq said: This is the narration of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and some people of Najran, from Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir, and Allah knows best which of these is correct.

He said: Then Dhu Nuwas marched against them with his army, invited them to Judaism, and gave them the choice between that or death. They chose death, so he dug the trench, burned them with fire, killed them by the sword, and mutilated them, until he had killed nearly twenty thousand of them. Concerning Dhu Nuwas and his army, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿Destroyed were the companions of the trench, the fire full of fuel, when they were sitting around it, and they were witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Witness over all things.﴾ [[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/34).]]

Thus did Muhammad ibn Ishaq mention in the Sirah that the one who killed the People of the Ditch (Ashab al-Ukhdud) was Dhu Nuwas.
