His name was Zur'ah, and during the time of his kingdom he was called Yusuf. He was the son of Tiban As'ad Abi Karib, and he was the Tubba' who attacked Madinah and covered (kasa) the Ka'bah. He took with him two rabbis from the Jews of Madinah, and through their hands the Jewish faith spread among the people of Yemen, as Ibn Ishaq related in detail. Dhu Nuwas killed twenty thousand people in the Ukhdud in a single morning, and none of them escaped except one man called Daws Dhu Tha'laban, who fled on horseback. They pursued him but could not catch him, so he went to Caesar, king of Syria, who wrote to the Negus, king of Abyssinia. He sent with him an army of Abyssinian Christians led by Aryat and Abrahah, and they rescued Yemen from the hands of the Jews. Dhu Nuwas fled, plunged into the sea, and drowned. The rule of Abyssinia remained in the hands of the Christians for seventy years. Then Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan al-Himyari rescued it from the hands of the Christians, after he sought help from Khosrow, king of Persia, who sent with him those in the prisons, who numbered about seven hundred. With them he conquered Yemen, and rule returned to Himyar. We will, God willing, mention a portion of this in the commentary on the surah: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant?﴾

Ibn Ishaq said: I was told by Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm that it was related that a man from the people of Najran, in the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab, dug in a ruin of Najran for some need he had, and found Abdullah ibn al-Thamir seated in a grave there, with his hand placed on a wound in his head, holding it with his hand. When they removed his hand from it, blood gushed out, and when they let his hand go, it returned to the wound and stopped the blood. On his hand was a ring on which was written: "My Lord is Allah." They wrote to Umar ibn al-Khattab informing him of the matter, and Umar wrote back to them: "Leave him in his state and return to him the grave in which he was." And they did so. [Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah li-Ibn Hisham (1/36).]

Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Dunya, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Abu Bilal al-Ash'ari related to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad related to us, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, who said: some of the people of knowledge told me that when Abu Musa conquered Isfahan, he found a wall of the walls of the city had collapsed. He rebuilt it, and it collapsed; he rebuilt it again, and it collapsed. It was said to him: "Beneath it is a righteous man." So he dug the foundation and found in it a man standing with a sword on which was written: "I am al-Harith ibn Mudad, I condemned the People of the Ditch." Abu Musa brought him out, rebuilt the wall, and it stood firm.

I say: He is al-Harith ibn Mudad ibn Amr ibn Mudad ibn Amr al-Jurhumi, one of the kings of Jurhum who held charge of the Ka'bah after the descendants of Nabt (in another manuscript: "Thabit") ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim. The son of this al-Harith is Amr ibn al-Harith ibn Mudad, the last of the kings of Jurhum in Makkah, when Khuza'ah expelled them and drove them out to Yemen. He is the one who said in the poem which Ibn Hisham said was the first poetry the Arabs composed:

"As if there had never been between al-Hajun and al-Safa a companion, and no one had chatted in Makkah by night.
Indeed, we were its people, but the turns of the nights and the ill-omened fortunes destroyed us."

This indicates that this story was long ago, after the time of Isma'il, peace be upon him, by about five hundred years or so. What Ibn Ishaq mentioned indicates that their story was in the period of interruption (fatrah) between Jesus and Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon them both, and this is more likely, and Allah knows best.

It is possible that such events occurred many times in the world, as Ibn Abi Hatim said:

My father related to us, Abu al-Yaman related to us, Safwan informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, who said: The Ukhdud in Yemen was in the time of Tubba', and in Constantinople in the time of Constantine, when the Christians turned their qibla away from the religion of the Messiah and monotheism. They made a furnace (atun), and the Christians who held to the religion of the Messiah and monotheism were thrown into it. And in Iraq, in the land of Babylon, there was Nebuchadnezzar, who set up the idol and commanded the people to prostrate to it. Daniel and his two companions, Azariah and Mishael, refused, so he kindled for them a furnace, put wood and fire into it, then threw them into it. Allah made it cool and safe for them, and rescued them from it, and He cast into it those who had transgressed against him, who were nine men, and the fire consumed them.

Asbat related from al-Suddi, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿Killed were the companions of the ditch﴾, that he said: The Ukhdud were three: a ditch in Iraq, a ditch in Syria, and a ditch in Yemen. Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

And from Muqatil, who said: The Ukhdud were three: one in Najran in Yemen, another in Syria, and another in Persia. As for the one in Syria, it was Antanunus the Roman; as for the one in Persia, it was Bukhtnassar; and as for the one in the land of the Arabs, it was Yusuf Dhu Nuwas. Regarding those in Persia and Syria, Allah did not send down any Qur'an, but He revealed concerning the one that was in Najran.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dashtaki related to us, Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿Killed were the companions of the ditch﴾, he said: We have heard that they were a people in the period of interruption (fatrah). When they saw the trial and evil that had befallen the people and that they had become factions, ﴿each faction rejoicing in what they have﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 53; al-Rum: 32], they withdrew to a village they settled in, and they remained devoted to the worship of Allah, ﴿sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and establishing prayer and giving zakah﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5]. This was their condition until a tyrant among the tyrants heard of them and was told their story. He sent for them and commanded them to worship the idols they had made, but they all refused and said: "We worship none but Allah alone, with no partner." He said to them: "If you do not worship these gods which I worship, I will kill you." They refused him, so he dug a trench of fire and stood them beside it, and the tyrant said to them: "Choose this, or what we are in." They said: "This is more beloved to us." Among them were women and children, and the children were frightened, so they said to them: "There is no fire after today." They threw themselves into it, and their souls were taken before the heat touched them, and the fire came out from its place and surrounded the tyrants, and Allah burned them with it. Concerning that, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Killed were the companions of the ditch, of the fire full of fuel, when they were sitting over it, and they were witnesses to what they did to the believers. And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is, over all things, Witness﴾.

Ibn Jarir related it: I was told from Ammar, from Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far, with similar wording [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/88)].

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, those who have tormented the believing men and believing women﴾: that is, burned them. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Abza.

﴿Then they did not repent﴾: that is, they did not desist from what they had done and did not regret what they had committed.

﴿Then for them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the Burning﴾. That is because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Look at this generosity and bounty! They killed His friends, and He calls them to repentance and forgiveness.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah, exalted is He, informs about His believing servants that ﴿for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ [[In the later copies: "abiding therein forever".]] in contrast to what He has prepared for His enemies of fire and blazing Hell. Therefore He says: ﴿That is the great triumph.﴾

Then He says: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe.﴾ That is, indeed His seizing and His vengeance upon His enemies, who denied His messengers and opposed His command, is severe, mighty and powerful. He is the Possessor of Strength, the Firm. Whatever He wills, happens as He wills in the twinkling of an eye, or it is even nearer. Therefore He says: ﴿Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats.﴾ That is, by His perfect strength and power He originates creation and then restores it as He originated it, with no one to prevent or repel Him. ﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Loving.﴾ That is, He forgives the sin of whoever repents to Him and submits to Him, whatever the sin may be.

Ibn 'Abbas and others said: "al-Wadud" means the Beloved. ﴿Owner of the Throne﴾ [That is: the Possessor of the Throne] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] the Glorious [[In manuscript A: "the Great".]], the Exalted above all creation.

As for ﴿al-Majid﴾, there are two readings: the nominative, as an attribute of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic; and the genitive, as an attribute of the Throne. Both meanings are sound.

﴿Doer of what He intends﴾ means: whatever He intends to do, He does, none can reverse His judgment, and He is not questioned about what He does, due to His greatness, dominance, wisdom and justice. As we have related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, that when he was on his deathbed he was asked: "Has the physician examined you?" He said: "Yes." They said: "What did he tell you?" He said: "He told me: Indeed, I am the Doer of what I intend."

* *

His saying: ﴿Has there reached you the account of the hosts, Pharaoh and Thamud?﴾ That is: has there reached you what Allah brought upon them of severe punishment, and the vengeance He sent down upon them, which no one could avert from them?

This is an affirmation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe.﴾ That is: when He seizes the wrongdoer, He seizes him with a painful and severe seizing, the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by a woman reciting: ﴿Has there reached you the account of the hosts,﴾ so he stood listening, and said: "Yes, it has come to me." [[This is mursal.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿Rather, those who disbelieve are in denial﴾ That is: they are in doubt, suspicion, disbelief and obstinacy. ﴿And Allah, from behind them, is encompassing﴾ That is: He is capable over them, dominant; they cannot escape Him nor overpower Him. ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Quran﴾ That is: great and noble. ﴿In a preserved tablet﴾ That is: it is preserved in the Highest Assembly, protected from addition, omission, distortion and alteration.

Ibn Jarir said: 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Qurrah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Harb ibn Surayj [[In manuscript A: "Shurayh".]] narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik regarding His saying: ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Quran in a preserved tablet﴾ he said: The Preserved Tablet which Allah mentioned, is on the forehead of Israfil. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/90).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salih narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to us, that Abu al-A'yas, namely 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Salman, said: Nothing that Allah has decreed—the Quran, what precedes it and what follows it—except that it is in the Preserved Tablet. The Preserved Tablet is between the two eyes of Israfil, and he is not permitted to look into it.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Indeed this glorious Quran is with Allah in a preserved tablet, from which He sends down what He wills upon whom He wills of His creation.

Al-Baghawi related through the route of Ishaq ibn Bishr, who said: Muqatil and Ibn Jurayj informed me, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: At the top of the Tablet is written: There is no god but Allah alone, His religion is Islam, and Muhammad is His servant and messenger. Whoever believes in Allah, affirms His promise and follows His messengers, He will admit into Paradise. He said: The Tablet is of white pearl, its length is the distance between heaven and earth, its width the distance between east and west, its edges are pearls and rubies, its covers are red ruby, its pen is light, its writing is light, and it is suspended by the Throne, and its origin is in the lap of an angel. [[Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (8/389).]]

Muqatil said: The Preserved Tablet is to the right of the Throne.

Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Minjab ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Ziyad ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Layth, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah created a preserved tablet of white pearl, its pages of red ruby, its pen is light and its book is light. For Allah in it every day are three hundred and sixty glances: He creates and provides, gives life and causes death, honors and humbles, and does what He wills." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/72). Ziyad and Layth ibn Abi Sulaym are weak; it is also reported as a statement of Ibn 'Abbas (mawquf), narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/316) through Bukayr ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, in similar wording.]]

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Buruj", and all praise is due to Allah. [[In manuscript A: "And Allah knows best".]]

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah, exalted is He, informs about His believing servants that ﴿for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ [[In the later copies: "abiding therein forever".]] in contrast to what He has prepared for His enemies of fire and blazing Hell. Therefore He says: ﴿That is the great triumph.﴾

He said: "He told me: Indeed, I am the Doer of what I intend."

[[This is mursal.]]

Ibn Jarir said: 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, Qurrah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Harb ibn Surayj [[In manuscript A: "Shurayh".]] narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Suhayb narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik regarding His saying: ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Quran in a preserved tablet﴾ he said: The Preserved Tablet which Allah mentioned, is on the forehead of Israfil. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (30/90).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salih narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to us, that Abu al-A'yas, namely 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Salman, said: Nothing that Allah has decreed—the Quran, what precedes it and what follows it—except that it is in the Preserved Tablet. The Preserved Tablet is between the two eyes of Israfil, and he is not permitted to look into it.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Indeed this glorious Quran is with Allah in a preserved tablet, from which He sends down what He wills upon whom He wills of His creation.

Al-Baghawi related through the route of Ishaq ibn Bishr, who said: Muqatil and Ibn Jurayj informed me, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: At the top of the Tablet is written: There is no god but Allah alone, His religion is Islam, and Muhammad is His servant and messenger. Whoever believes in Allah, affirms His promise and follows His messengers, He will admit into Paradise. He said: The Tablet is of white pearl, its length is the distance between heaven and earth, its width the distance between east and west, its edges are pearls and rubies, its covers are red ruby, its pen is light, its writing is light, and it is suspended by the Throne, and its origin is in the lap of an angel. [[Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi (8/389).]]

Muqatil said: The Preserved Tablet is to the right of the Throne.

Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Minjab ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Ziyad ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Layth, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah created a preserved tablet of white pearl, its pages of red ruby, its pen is light and its book is light. For Allah in it every day are three hundred and sixty glances: He creates and provides, gives life and causes death, honors and humbles, and does what He wills." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/72). Ziyad and Layth ibn Abi Sulaym are weak; it is also reported as a statement of Ibn 'Abbas (mawquf), narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/316) through Bukayr ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, in similar wording.]]

End of the tafsir of Surah "al-Buruj", and all praise is due to Allah. [[In manuscript A: "And Allah knows best".]]

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says: Allah, exalted is He, informs about His believing servants that ﴿for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ [[In the later copies: "abiding therein forever".]] in contrast to what He has prepared for His enemies of fire and blazing Hell. Therefore He says: ﴿That is the great triumph.﴾

Then He says: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe.﴾ That is, indeed His seizing and His vengeance upon His enemies, who denied His messengers and opposed His command, is severe, mighty and powerful. He is the Possessor of Strength, the Firm. Whatever He wills, happens as He wills in the twinkling of an eye, or it is even nearer. Therefore He says: ﴿Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats.﴾ That is, by His perfect strength and power He originates creation and then restores it as He originated it, with no one to prevent or repel Him. ﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Loving.﴾ That is, He forgives the sin of whoever repents to Him and submits to Him, whatever the sin may be.

Ibn 'Abbas and others said: "al-Wadud" means the Beloved. ﴿Owner of the Throne﴾ [That is: the Possessor of the Throne] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] the Glorious [[In manuscript A: "the Great".]], the Exalted above all creation.

As for ﴿al-Majid﴾, there are two readings: the nominative, as an attribute of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic; and the genitive, as an attribute of the Throne. Both meanings are sound.

﴿Doer of what He intends﴾ means: whatever He intends to do, He does, none can reverse His judgment, and He is not questioned about what He does, due to His greatness, dominance, wisdom and justice. As we have related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, that when he was on his deathbed he was asked: "Has the physician examined you?" He said: "Yes." They said: "What did he tell you?" He said: "He told me: Indeed, I am the Doer of what I intend."

* *

His saying: ﴿Has there reached you the account of the hosts, Pharaoh and Thamud?﴾ That is: has there reached you what Allah brought upon them of severe punishment, and the vengeance He sent down upon them, which no one could avert from them?

This is an affirmation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe.﴾ That is: when He seizes the wrongdoer, He seizes him with a painful and severe seizing, the seizing of the Mighty, the Omnipotent.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) passed by a woman reciting: ﴿Has there reached you the account of the hosts,﴾ so he stood listening, and said: "Yes, it has come to me." [[This is mursal.]]
